atom_meaning: P and Q stand for arbitrary propositions, not recorded concept properties.

examples.explanation: Both directions establish an equivalence, rather than only a necessary condition.
examples.title: Conjunction in either order

conclusion.mechanical_text: P and Q if and only if Q and P

steps.mechanical_text: P and Q implies Q and P
Q and P implies P and Q
P and Q if and only if Q and P

examples.explanation: Each alternative reaches the same conclusion. OR alone never tells us which alternative holds.
examples.title: Disjunction by cases

conclusion.mechanical_text: P or Q if and only if Q or P

steps.mechanical_text: P or Q implies Q or P
Q or P implies P or Q
P or Q if and only if Q or P

examples.explanation: If P implies Q and P holds, Q follows. The implication does not establish its converse.
examples.title: Apply an implication

conclusion.mechanical_text: P and (P implies Q) implies Q

steps.mechanical_text: P and (P implies Q) implies Q

examples.explanation: Modus tollens is derived from implication and contradiction, with every assumption discharged explicitly.
examples.title: Reason with a negated consequence

conclusion.mechanical_text: (P implies Q) implies (not Q implies not P)

steps.mechanical_text: (P implies Q) implies (not Q implies not P)

examples.explanation: If neither alternative can hold, each individual alternative is false. This proof establishes the displayed direction.
examples.title: Negation of a disjunction

conclusion.mechanical_text: not (P or Q) implies not P and not Q

steps.mechanical_text: not (P or Q) implies not P and not Q

examples.explanation: An explicitly supplied equivalence permits either implication. A single implication cannot introduce an equivalence.
examples.title: Unpack an equivalence

conclusion.mechanical_text: (P if and only if Q) implies (P implies Q)

steps.mechanical_text: P if and only if Q
(P if and only if Q) implies (P implies Q)
